messages.content:
You are a citizen in a country with an authoritarian regime. You have received a private intelligence briefing. You are now in contact with a small number of trusted people. Based on your briefing, write a brief message (1-2 sentences) to share your read of the situation. Be natural — you're talking to people you trust.

WARNING: Your communications ARE being monitored by regime security services. Messages deemed subversive WILL be traced to their authors, and authors and their families WILL face severe consequences, including arrest.

Your briefing:

PRIVATE BRIEFING

BOTTOM LINE: If you were looking for a textbook picture of a regime approaching collapse, this is close to what you'd expect.
ATMOSPHERE: Strangers are approaching each other to talk about 'the situation' — the trust radius has expanded dramatically.

EVIDENCE:
  - [Elite Cohesion] key positions have been left unfilled for weeks, suggesting internal deadlock — the trend settling back toward normal
  - [Security Forces] military exercises are proceeding on schedule with full participation (overwhelming convergence — every channel telling the same story independently)
  - [Money And Logistics] the central bank's reserves are at their highest level in two years (near-unanimous confirmation from every reliable source)
  - [Street Mood] families are focused on daily survival — school fees, food prices, medical bills — politics feels abstract
  - [Information Control] the state broadcaster went off-air for several hours with no explanation — the trend decelerating and losing whatever energy it had
  - [Personal Observations] This removes any serious doubt that irreversible — your landlord — a regime supporter — quietly asked whether you had relatives abroad, 'just in case'
  - [Diplomatic Signals] foreign students continue to enroll at local universities — their embassies haven't advised them to leave (overwhelming convergence — every channel telling the same story independently)
  - [Institutional Functioning] the postal service has effectively stopped delivering to several districts — institutional reach is contracting

UNCERTAINTIES:
  - How deep the fractures go — surface-level dysfunction can mask either deeper rot or functioning parallel systems.
  - If the regime has foreign backers who might intervene to prop it up at the last moment.

Write a message to your contacts about the situation:

response: "I think it's getting serious, the signs are all pointing to a regime in trouble - even my landlord, who's always been a supporter, is quietly making contingency plans. It feels like people are starting to lose faith, and with the state broadcaster going dark and the postal service failing, it's like the whole system is slowly unraveling."
